# Ordinary proof of the MathDB 349441 counterexample

AI-assisted DRAFT. Zero accepted credit. No priority claim.

## A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering

### Status and abstract

This is an AI-assisted research draft prepared with OpenAI Codex. No human authorship or affiliation is asserted. Acceptance, independent manuscript review, and any campaign credit remain with the project root; accepted credit is zero. No priority claim is made.

Estrada and Mugnolo conjectured that the hubs-repelling Kirchhoff index dominates the ordinary Kirchhoff index, which in turn dominates the hubs-attracting index [1, Conjecture 4.13]. For the spectral quantity in their Lemma 4.6, the graph consisting of K₆ with a pendant path of five edges has R₁ = 1696684/14035 < 370/3 = R₀. We give exact rational inverse certificates and a Lean dossier with uniqueness proofs over both the rationals and the reals. The independently reviewed experiment has no spectral failures on all 12,103 connected graphs of orders 5 through 8, consistent with the source's reported computation. Global minimality remains open: the smallest spectral counterexample has order between 9 and 11.

The source's potential, Moore-Penrose, and spectral descriptions are not mutually equivalent on irregular graphs. We explain the distinction without claiming credit for these observations. The spectral counterexample persists after that distinction is made; it is the substantive result reported here.

### 1. Source objects and the precise question

Let G be a finite simple connected unweighted graph on n ≥ 2 vertices. Write A for its adjacency matrix, dᵢ for its positive degrees, K = diag(dᵢ), and 1 for the all-ones column. The biased Laplacian in [1, (3.8)] is defined by the following entries (we also allow α = 0):

cα(i) = Σⱼ Aᵢⱼ(dᵢ/dⱼ)^α,     Lα = diag(cα) − K^α A K^(−α).

Thus Lα1 = 0 and L₀ is the ordinary combinatorial Laplacian. The source uses α = 1 for hubs-repelling and α = −1 for hubs-attracting. Definition 4.1 defines resistance as a potential drop divided by the imposed current. Lemma 4.2, equation (4.3), instead specifies a Moore-Penrose matrix expression. For X = Lα⁺ it is

Ωα(i,j) = Xᵢᵢ + Xⱼⱼ − Xᵢⱼ − Xⱼᵢ;     Rαᴹᴾ = Σᵢ<ⱼ Ωα(i,j).

The sum is Definition 4.5, equation (4.15). Both off-diagonal entries are essential, since X need not be symmetric. Lemma 4.6, equation (4.16), asserts the different spectral expression

Rαˢᵖ = n Σₖ₌₂ⁿ 1/ρα,ₖ = n tr(Lα#).

Here 0 = ρα,₁ < ρα,₂ ≤ ⋯ ≤ ρα,ₙ are the eigenvalues and # denotes the group inverse. Section 3 below justifies this spectral interpretation independently of the source's Moore-Penrose argument. Conjecture 4.13, equation (4.25), asserts R₁ ≥ R₀ ≥ R₋₁, with equality if and only if G is regular. Violating the first inequality already refutes that universal assertion, regardless of the interpretation of its equality clause.

## 2. Why the three source descriptions separate

### The physical equation has a compatibility obstruction

Set wᵢ = dᵢ^(−2α). For adjacent i,j the identity wᵢ(dᵢ/dⱼ)^α = (dᵢdⱼ)^(−α) is symmetric in i,j. Consequently wᵀLα = 0. The potential equation in the proof of Lemma 4.2, namely LαV = I(eᵢ − eⱼ) [1, (4.7)], requires I(wᵢ − wⱼ) = 0. For nonzero I and α = ±1 this requires equal degrees at the source and sink. An irregular graph has unequal-degree pairs, so this equation does not define an all-pairs physical resistance index.

This is a necessary compatibility condition for the source's equation, rather than a proposed repair of its directional Ohm-law or antisymmetry assumptions. In particular, we do not claim that every possible corrected physical resistance model is refuted by our graph. For the witness below, w₀ − w₁₀ = −35/36 when α = 1, giving an explicit incompatible pair.

### The non-orthogonal similarity does not preserve Penrose inversion

The source diagonalizes Lα using a non-orthogonal change of basis and treats the correspondingly transformed reciprocal-eigenvalue matrix as its Moore-Penrose inverse in the proof of Lemma 4.2; Lemma 4.6 then uses its trace. Similarity preserves the group-inverse equations, but in general it does not preserve the two transpose equations defining the Moore-Penrose inverse. Orthogonal similarity would preserve those equations; the degree scaling used here is not orthogonal on irregular graphs.

Accordingly, (4.3) and Lemma 4.6's formula (4.16) give different numbers. The source's equation numbered (4.6) is the vertex potential-balance equation, not the spectral formula; this numbering distinction matters when describing the inconsistency. For our witness at α = 1 the true Moore-Penrose pair sum is 515538204/7137235, whereas the spectral value is 1696684/14035. The dossier contains proofs that the group inverse is not a Penrose inverse at this witness. These observations receive no separate discovery credit.

### The reported computation diagnoses the intended numerical quantity

Before Conjecture 4.13, the authors report computations on more than 12,000 connected graphs with 5 ≤ n ≤ 8. The independent frozen review [R] checked the connected graph datasets exactly and obtained the following counts. No equality-versus-regularity failures were found in either reading.

At n = 5 the graph K₄ with a pendant vertex already has R₁ᴹᴾ = 33856/4317 < 17/2 = R₀. The Moore-Penrose reading therefore contradicts the source's reported exhaustive data inside its stated range. By contrast the spectral reading passes every graph in that range. This strongly identifies the computed quantity as spectral; the authors' implementation was not recovered, so this remains an inference about their code. The review also enumerated all connected graphs of orders 2, 3, and 4. Taken together, these checks establish the diagnostic statement that the spectral ordering holds through n = 8. This finite enumeration is supporting computational evidence, not a Lean theorem or a proof of the conjecture.

## 3. The eleven-vertex counterexample

### Theorem and graph

Let H have vertices 0,…,10. Join every pair in {0,…,5}, and add edges {0,6}, {6,7}, {7,8}, {8,9}, {9,10}. This is K₆ with a pendant five-edge path, and it is simple and connected. Its degree sequence is (6,5,5,5,5,5,2,2,2,2,1). Then

R₁ˢᵖ(H) = 1696684/14035 < 370/3 = R₀(H).

Hence the spectral reading of Conjecture 4.13 is false. Independently, R₁ᴹᴾ(H) = 515538204/7137235 < 370/3, so its literal Moore-Penrose reading is false as well. This is one spectral-ordering counterexample, with a secondary source inconsistency; it is not two claimed results.

### Ordinary proof of the spectral correspondence

Let W = diag(w). The matrix WLα is a symmetric weighted Laplacian whose edge conductances are (dᵢdⱼ)^(−α). For any real x, xᵀWLαx is the sum over edges of (dᵢdⱼ)^(−α)(xᵢ − xⱼ)². It is nonnegative, and connectedness makes its kernel precisely the constants. Since W is positive diagonal, S = W^(1/2)LαW^(−1/2) = K^(−α)LαK^α is symmetric positive semidefinite with one-dimensional kernel. Thus Lα is diagonalizable, zero is simple, and every other eigenvalue is positive.

In a diagonalization of Lα, replace the simple zero eigenvalue by zero and every other eigenvalue by its reciprocal. The resulting matrix satisfies LGL = L, GLG = G, and LG = GL. Uniqueness of the group inverse (proved below and in Lean) identifies it with Lα#. Trace is similarity invariant, so tr(Lα#) = Σₖ₌₂ⁿ 1/ρα,ₖ. This argument justifies the spectral reading without using any similarity law for the Moore-Penrose inverse. The eigenvalue argument in this paragraph is ordinary mathematics, not part of the Lean bridge.

### Exact values and the decisive inequality

The rational certificates give the following values; the α = −1 row entries come from the independent exact review, while the formal refutation requires only α = 0 and 1.

Cross multiplication gives R₀ − R₁ˢᵖ = 102898/42105 > 0. No floating-point eigenvalue estimate is involved. As an independent check on the ordinary value, each clique pair has resistance 1/3, yielding 5 in total. Among vertices 0,6,…,10 the path contributes 35. For a clique vertex i ≠ 0 and a path vertex at distance t from 0, resistance is 1/3 + t. The 25 such pairs contribute 5(5/3 + 15) = 250/3. Their sum is 370/3. Section 4 explains how the biased value is certified by finite rational identities.

## 4. Exact certificates and uniqueness

### A compact description of all matrix entries

The full 11 × 11 rational Laplacians, Moore-Penrose inverses, group inverses, and intermediate products for α = 0,1 appear explicitly in formal/Certificates.lean. The independent review's witness-exact.json also supplies all three α values as arrays of rational strings. The following formulas describe these large matrices without printing hundreds of entries in the paper. They specify every entry once the displayed graph and degree sequence are fixed.

Put P = 1wᵀ/(wᵀ1), U = 11ᵀ/n, and T = wwᵀ/(wᵀw). Then define

G = (Lα + P)⁻¹ − P,           M = (I − U)G(I − T).

The rank-one P is the spectral projection onto ker Lα along im Lα: P² = P and LαP = PLα = 0. On the zero eigenspace, Lα + P acts as the identity; on every other eigenspace it acts as Lα. It is therefore invertible. This gives LG = GL = I − P and the three group-inverse identities. Since im L is the orthogonal complement of w and ker L = span{1}, projection yields LM = I − T and ML = I − U. Both are orthogonal projections; hence LML = L and MLM = M, with both LM and ML symmetric. This proves all four Penrose conditions for M.

### Finite checking and a sample of the construction

Every construction step can use exact rational Gaussian elimination. For α = 1, w = (1/36,1/25,1/25,1/25,1/25,1/25,1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4,1), and wᵀ1 = 401/180. The first row of L₁ is (9,−6/5,−6/5,−6/5,−6/5,−6/5,−3,0,0,0,0); an ordinary clique vertex has diagonal 29/6, entry −5/6 to vertex 0, and four entries −1. Vertex 6 has row entries −1/3 at 0, 4/3 at 6, and −1 at 7. These rules and the edge formula in Section 1 determine L₁ completely.

The formal certificate does not trust a Gaussian-elimination program. It checks the resulting matrix equations and index sums in the kernel using rational arithmetic. Separate certificates verify the four Penrose equations for M₀,M₁ and the three group-inverse equations for G₀,G₁. The graph module proves that its Laplacians equal the displayed L₀,L₁ and that the witness is connected. The index equalities then reduce to exact rational identities.

### Why the inverse cannot be chosen differently

Here is an algebraic uniqueness proof, valid over the reals or rationals. If X,Y are Penrose inverses of A, then (AX)(AY) = AY and (AY)(AX) = AX. Transposing the first identity, using symmetry of AX and AY, identifies AX = AY. Similarly the symmetric products XA and YA agree. Thus X = XAX = YAX = YAY = Y. If X,Y are group inverses, commutation gives AX = (AYA)X = Y(AXA) = YA = AY; then X = XAX = XAY = AXY = AYY = YAY = Y. This removes all inverse-choice ambiguity. In particular, existential inverse data in the conjecture cannot avoid the certified strict inequality. Both uniqueness arguments are formalized over the rationals in Basic.lean and repeated over the reals in RealBridge.lean.

Global spectral minimality remains open in [9,11]. The eigenvalue bridge here is ordinary mathematics; the Lean endpoint is the unique group-inverse trace. Full rational matrices are in formal/Certificates.lean and sources/kirchhoff-review-r1/outputs/witness-exact.json.

# Reproduce the dossier

Safely extract kirchhoff-source-only.zip into a NEW empty directory. Reject absolute paths, parent traversal, symlinks, duplicate member names and compiled artifacts. scripts/safe_extract.py implements these checks. Run it as `python3 -I scripts/safe_extract.py kirchhoff-source-only.zip fresh-replay` from the dossier directory. All writes must remain in this lane during the assigned run.

Set LEAN_BIN to the **executable**, for this machine `/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/dlp-research/.tools/lean-4.34.1-linux/bin/lean`. Set LEAN_PACKAGES to `/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research/frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/formal/.lake/packages`, or an equivalent read-only package cache. Required pins: Lean 4.34.1 commit 5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52; mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612. sources/lake-manifest.json records all package revisions. Provision these outside the driver; it neither downloads nor mutates dependencies. The cached package contents are an external trust input, not independently rebuilt here.

Inside the extraction, run `python3 -I replay.py`. Existing oleans anywhere inside the extraction cause refusal. The driver verifies source-hashes.json, checks the exact Lean version through its watchdog, strictly builds Basic, Certificates, Graph, RealBridge, and Audit with `-j1 -DwarningAsError=true`, and runs leanchecker for each. Audit is command-only tooling; its audit selects all 176 declarations in the four proof modules, by module identity, with full type and body ASTs including opaque bodies, safety and partiality flags, and transitive axiom lists. Only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound are allowed. No local axiom is allowed.

It then checks the reviewer's three positive proofs of control negations, plus three expected-failure false-claim attempts. Expected failures alone can be elaboration failures, so use the positive semantic controls as substantive evidence. No killed process counts as rejection. Every invocation, including `--version` and leanchecker, passes through scripts/run.py: at most two CPU affinities; 120-second CPU limit; 140-second wall limit; MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2; 6 GiB sampled aggregate process-group RSS cap at 50 ms intervals. Shared pages may be counted twice across processes, conservatively. This is a sampled cap, not a hard virtual-address-space limit. The runner waits for its process and kills its process group on limit violation. Calls run sequentially, with no parallel heavy processes.

Receipts are written under receipts/, full logs under logs/, temporary files under outputs/ inside the extraction. `receipts/replay.json` appears only after every stage passes. This source packet is self-contained for local proof source and harness, not for Lean/mathlib binaries. No network access is needed for replay.

Manuscript: paper/manuscript.json contains the prose source; paper/render.py renders it with ReportLab and Liberation Serif fonts. Install ReportLab in a lane-local directory (this run used outputs/python-libs), or provide it through Python. The six-page PDF is paper/kirchhoff-draft.pdf. The QA PNGs and receipt record inspection of every final page. The full dossier retains exact copied source bodies and historical HTTP receipts; these are frozen evidence, not newly fetched sources. PROOF.md contains the ordinary proof.

The source-only ZIP carries text/Lean proof source, exact matrices and evidence, the manuscript source, and replay harness, with no compiled modules, rendered manuscript PDF, or environment (upstream source PDFs are retained). The full ZIP additionally carries the PDF, final QA images, replay logs/receipts, summary/results and manifests. It omits fresh-replay compiled oleans and the lane-local Python installation. Source ZIP integrity is external in manifests/archives.json; full ZIP integrity is in manifests/delivery.json, outside the ZIP to avoid a circular hash.

Both mathematical and literature limitations are explicit in the paper. Zero accepted credit; root final replay and manuscript acceptance remain pending. This lane performs no publication, upload, ledger update, or external messaging.

files.formal/Audit.lean:
import RealBridge
import Lean
open Lean Elab Command
set_option pp.all true
run_cmd do
  let env ← getEnv
  let mut count : Nat := 0
  for (n,c) in env.constants.toList do
    let some idx := env.getModuleIdxFor? n | continue
    let m := env.header.moduleNames[idx.toNat]!
    if (["Basic", "Certificates", "Graph", "RealBridge"] : List String).contains m.toString then
      count := count + 1
      let ax ← Lean.collectAxioms n
      logInfo m!"DECL|{n}|MODULE|{m}|UNSAFE|{c.isUnsafe}|PARTIAL|{c.isPartial}|AXIOMS|{ax.toList}"
      logInfo m!"FULL_TYPE_AST|{repr c.type}"
      logInfo m!"FULL_BODY_AST_value?_true|{repr (c.value? true)}"
      if c.isUnsafe || c.isPartial then throwError "bad safety {n}"
      match c with
      | .axiomInfo _ => throwError "local axiom {n}"
      | _ => pure ()
      match c with
      | .inductInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|inductive|{n}"
      | .ctorInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|constructor|{n}"
      | .recInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|recursor|{n}"
      | _ => if !(c.value? true).isSome then throwError "missing body {n}"
      for x in ax do
        if !([``propext, ``Classical.choice, ``Quot.sound] : List Name).contains x then
          throwError "disallowed axiom {x} in {n}"
  logInfo m!"AUDITED_LOCAL_DECLARATIONS|{count}"
files.formal/Basic.lean:
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Trace
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
set_option maxRecDepth 100000
set_option maxHeartbeats 8000000
namespace Kirchhoff
open Matrix
abbrev Mat (n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ
def Penrose {n : ℕ} (A X : Mat n) : Prop :=
 A * X * A = A ∧ X * A * X = X ∧ (A * X).transpose = A * X ∧ (X * A).transpose = X * A
def GroupInverse {n : ℕ} (A X : Mat n) : Prop :=
 A * X * A = A ∧ X * A * X = X ∧ A * X = X * A
end Kirchhoff
namespace Kirchhoff
open Matrix
theorem penrose_unique {n : ℕ} {A X Y : Mat n} (hX : Penrose A X) (hY : Penrose A Y) : X = Y := by
 obtain ⟨axa, xax, axsym, xasym⟩ := hX
 obtain ⟨aya, yay, aysym, yasym⟩ := hY
 have p : A * X * (A * Y) = A * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, axa]
 have q : A * Y * (A * X) = A * X := by rw [← mul_assoc, aya]
 have pt := congrArg Matrix.transpose p
 rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, axsym, aysym] at pt
 have axay : A * X = A * Y := q.symm.trans pt
 have r : X * A * (Y * A) = X * A := by rw [mul_assoc X A, ← mul_assoc A Y, aya]
 have s : Y * A * (X * A) = Y * A := by rw [mul_assoc Y A, ← mul_assoc A X, axa]
 have rt := congrArg Matrix.transpose r
 rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, xasym, yasym] at rt
 have xaya : X * A = Y * A := rt.symm.trans s
 calc
  X = X * A * X := xax.symm
  _ = Y * A * X := by rw [xaya]
  _ = Y * (A * Y) := by rw [mul_assoc, axay]
  _ = Y := by simpa only [mul_assoc] using yay

theorem group_unique {n : ℕ} {A X Y : Mat n} (hX : GroupInverse A X) (hY : GroupInverse A Y) : X = Y := by
 obtain ⟨axa, xax, ax⟩ := hX
 obtain ⟨aya, yay, ay⟩ := hY
 have p : A * X * (A * Y) = A * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, axa]
 have q : A * Y * (A * X) = A * X := by rw [← mul_assoc, aya]
 have axay : A * X = A * Y := by
  calc
   A * X = (A * Y * A) * X := by rw [aya]
   _ = Y * (A * X * A) := by rw [ay]; simp only [mul_assoc]; rw [← ax]
   _ = Y * A := by rw [axa]
   _ = A * Y := ay.symm
 calc
  X = X * A * X := xax.symm
  _ = X * (A * X) := mul_assoc _ _ _
  _ = X * (A * Y) := by rw [axay]
  _ = (A * X) * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, ← ax]
  _ = (A * Y) * Y := by rw [axay]
  _ = Y * A * Y := by rw [ay]
  _ = Y := by simpa only [mul_assoc] using yay
end Kirchhoff
files.formal/Graph.lean:
import Certificates
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected
import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Int.Parity
namespace Kirchhoff
open Matrix
set_option maxRecDepth 100000
set_option maxHeartbeats 8000000
structure Graph (n : ℕ) where
 adj : Fin n → Fin n → Bool
 symm : ∀ i j, adj i j = adj j i
 loopless : ∀ i, adj i i = false

def Graph.simple {n} (g : Graph n) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) where
 Adj i j := g.adj i j = true
 symm := ⟨fun i j h => by rwa [g.symm] at h⟩
 loopless := ⟨fun i h => by simp [g.loopless] at h⟩

instance {n} (g : Graph n) : DecidableRel g.simple.Adj :=
 fun i j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (g.adj i j = true))

def degree {n} (g : Graph n) (i : Fin n) : ℕ := ∑ j, if g.adj i j then 1 else 0

def Kpow {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) : Mat n := Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (degree g i : ℚ) ^ a)
def weight {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) (i j : Fin n) : ℚ :=
 if g.adj i j then (degree g i : ℚ) ^ a * (degree g j : ℚ) ^ (-a) else 0
def laplacian {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) : Mat n :=
 fun i j => (if i = j then ∑ k, weight g a i k else 0) - weight g a i j

def witness : Graph 11 where
 adj i j := decide ((i.val < 6 ∧ j.val < 6 ∧ i ≠ j) ∨
   (i = 0 ∧ j = 6) ∨ (j = 0 ∧ i = 6) ∨
   (6 ≤ i.val ∧ i.val + 1 = j.val) ∨ (6 ≤ j.val ∧ j.val + 1 = i.val))
 symm := by decide +kernel
 loopless := by decide +kernel

theorem witness_connected : witness.simple.Connected := by
 rw [SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable]
 refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
 have r6 : witness.simple.Reachable 0 6 := SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 have r7 : witness.simple.Reachable 0 7 := r6.trans (SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel))
 have r8 : witness.simple.Reachable 0 8 := r7.trans (SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel))
 have r9 : witness.simple.Reachable 0 9 := r8.trans (SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel))
 have r10 : witness.simple.Reachable 0 10 := r9.trans (SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel))
 intro i
 fin_cases i
 · exact SimpleGraph.Reachable.refl _
 · exact SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 · exact SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 · exact SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 · exact SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 · exact SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable (by decide +kernel)
 · exact r6
 · exact r7
 · exact r8
 · exact r9
 · exact r10

theorem lapZero : laplacian witness 0 = LZero := by decide +kernel
theorem lapOne : laplacian witness 1 = LOne := by decide +kernel
noncomputable def mp {n} (A : Mat n) : Mat n := by
 classical
 exact if h : ∃ X, Penrose A X then Classical.choose h else 0
noncomputable def gi {n} (A : Mat n) : Mat n := by
 classical
 exact if h : ∃ X, GroupInverse A X then Classical.choose h else 0

theorem mp_eq {n} {A X : Mat n} (h : Penrose A X) : mp A = X := by
 unfold mp
 rw [dite_eq_left ⟨X,h⟩]
 exact penrose_unique (Classical.choose_spec (show ∃ X, Penrose A X from ⟨X,h⟩)) h

theorem gi_eq {n} {A X : Mat n} (h : GroupInverse A X) : gi A = X := by
 unfold gi
 rw [dite_eq_left ⟨X,h⟩]
 exact group_unique (Classical.choose_spec (show ∃ X, GroupInverse A X from ⟨X,h⟩)) h
noncomputable def resistance {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) (i j : Fin n) : ℚ :=
 let X := mp (laplacian g a)
 X i i + X j j - X i j - X j i
noncomputable def indexMP {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) : ℚ := pairIndex (mp (laplacian g a))
noncomputable def indexSpec {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) : ℚ := spectralIndex (gi (laplacian g a))
def Regular {n} (g : Graph n) : Prop := ∃ d, ∀ i, degree g i = d

def Conjecture (R : {n : ℕ} → Graph n → ℤ → ℚ) : Prop :=
 ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → ∀ g : Graph n, g.simple.Connected → ∀ a : ℤ, a = 1 ∨ a = -1 →
 (if a = 1 then R g 0 ≤ R g a else R g a ≤ R g 0) ∧
 (R g a = R g 0 ↔ Regular g)

theorem mp_value_zero : indexMP witness 0 = 370/3 := by
 rw [indexMP, lapZero, mp_eq validMPZero, mp0]
theorem mp_value_one : indexMP witness 1 = 515538204/7137235 := by
 rw [indexMP, lapOne, mp_eq validMPOne, mp1]
theorem spec_value_zero : indexSpec witness 0 = 370/3 := by
 rw [indexSpec, lapZero, gi_eq validGIZero, gi0]
theorem spec_value_one : indexSpec witness 1 = 1696684/14035 := by
 rw [indexSpec, lapOne, gi_eq validGIOne, gi1]
theorem refuteMP : ¬ Conjecture @indexMP := by
 intro h
 have bad := (h 11 (by decide +kernel) witness witness_connected 1 (Or.inl rfl)).1
 simp only [ite_true] at bad
 rw [mp_value_zero, mp_value_one] at bad
 norm_num at bad
theorem refuteSpec : ¬ Conjecture @indexSpec := by
 intro h
 have bad := (h 11 (by decide +kernel) witness witness_connected 1 (Or.inl rfl)).1
 simp only [ite_true] at bad
 rw [spec_value_zero, spec_value_one] at bad
 norm_num at bad
end Kirchhoff
namespace Kirchhoff
open Matrix
theorem resistance_sum {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) :
 indexMP g a = ∑ i, ∑ j, if i < j then resistance g a i j else 0 := rfl

def adjacency {n} (g : Graph n) : Mat n := fun i j => if g.adj i j then 1 else 0

theorem laplacian_source_formula {n} (g : Graph n) (a : ℤ) :
 laplacian g a = Matrix.diagonal (fun i => ∑ k, weight g a i k) -
 Kpow g a * adjacency g * Kpow g (-a) := by
 ext i j
 simp only [laplacian, Kpow, Matrix.diagonal_mul, Matrix.mul_diagonal, Matrix.sub_apply,
  Matrix.diagonal_apply, adjacency, weight]

theorem primary_strict : indexMP witness 1 < indexMP witness 0 := by
 rw [mp_value_one, mp_value_zero]
 norm_num

theorem secondary_strict : indexSpec witness 1 < indexSpec witness 0 := by
 rw [spec_value_one, spec_value_zero]
 norm_num

import Graph
import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Rat
namespace KirchhoffReal
open Matrix
abbrev Mat (n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
def Penrose {n : ℕ} (A X : Mat n) : Prop :=
 A * X * A = A ∧ X * A * X = X ∧ (A * X).transpose = A * X ∧ (X * A).transpose = X * A
def GroupInverse {n : ℕ} (A X : Mat n) : Prop :=
 A * X * A = A ∧ X * A * X = X ∧ A * X = X * A
end KirchhoffReal
namespace KirchhoffReal
open Matrix
theorem penrose_unique {n : ℕ} {A X Y : Mat n} (hX : Penrose A X) (hY : Penrose A Y) : X = Y := by
 obtain ⟨axa, xax, axsym, xasym⟩ := hX
 obtain ⟨aya, yay, aysym, yasym⟩ := hY
 have p : A * X * (A * Y) = A * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, axa]
 have q : A * Y * (A * X) = A * X := by rw [← mul_assoc, aya]
 have pt := congrArg Matrix.transpose p
 rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, axsym, aysym] at pt
 have axay : A * X = A * Y := q.symm.trans pt
 have r : X * A * (Y * A) = X * A := by rw [mul_assoc X A, ← mul_assoc A Y, aya]
 have s : Y * A * (X * A) = Y * A := by rw [mul_assoc Y A, ← mul_assoc A X, axa]
 have rt := congrArg Matrix.transpose r
 rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, xasym, yasym] at rt
 have xaya : X * A = Y * A := rt.symm.trans s
 calc
  X = X * A * X := xax.symm
  _ = Y * A * X := by rw [xaya]
  _ = Y * (A * Y) := by rw [mul_assoc, axay]
  _ = Y := by simpa only [mul_assoc] using yay

theorem group_unique {n : ℕ} {A X Y : Mat n} (hX : GroupInverse A X) (hY : GroupInverse A Y) : X = Y := by
 obtain ⟨axa, xax, ax⟩ := hX
 obtain ⟨aya, yay, ay⟩ := hY
 have p : A * X * (A * Y) = A * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, axa]
 have q : A * Y * (A * X) = A * X := by rw [← mul_assoc, aya]
 have axay : A * X = A * Y := by
  calc
   A * X = (A * Y * A) * X := by rw [aya]
   _ = Y * (A * X * A) := by rw [ay]; simp only [mul_assoc]; rw [← ax]
   _ = Y * A := by rw [axa]
   _ = A * Y := ay.symm
 calc
  X = X * A * X := xax.symm
  _ = X * (A * X) := mul_assoc _ _ _
  _ = X * (A * Y) := by rw [axay]
  _ = (A * X) * Y := by rw [← mul_assoc, ← ax]
  _ = (A * Y) * Y := by rw [axay]
  _ = Y * A * Y := by rw [ay]
  _ = Y := by simpa only [mul_assoc] using yay
end KirchhoffReal
namespace KirchhoffReal
open Matrix
noncomputable def liftQ {n} (A : Kirchhoff.Mat n) : Mat n := A.map (algebraMap ℚ ℝ)
theorem lift_mul {n} (A B : Kirchhoff.Mat n) : liftQ (A * B) = liftQ A * liftQ B := by
 exact Matrix.map_mul

theorem lift_penrose {n} {A X : Kirchhoff.Mat n} (h : Kirchhoff.Penrose A X) :
 Penrose (liftQ A) (liftQ X) := by
 obtain ⟨h1,h2,h3,h4⟩ := h
 refine ⟨?_,?_,?_,?_⟩
 · simpa only [lift_mul] using congrArg liftQ h1
 · simpa only [lift_mul] using congrArg liftQ h2
 · simpa only [lift_mul, liftQ, Matrix.transpose_map, Matrix.map_mul] using congrArg liftQ h3
 · simpa only [lift_mul, liftQ, Matrix.transpose_map, Matrix.map_mul] using congrArg liftQ h4

theorem lift_group {n} {A X : Kirchhoff.Mat n} (h : Kirchhoff.GroupInverse A X) :
 GroupInverse (liftQ A) (liftQ X) := by
 obtain ⟨h1,h2,h3⟩ := h
 refine ⟨?_,?_,?_⟩
 · simpa only [lift_mul] using congrArg liftQ h1
 · simpa only [lift_mul] using congrArg liftQ h2
 · simpa only [lift_mul] using congrArg liftQ h3

def pairIndex {n} (X : Mat n) : ℝ := ∑ i, ∑ j, if i < j then X i i + X j j - X i j - X j i else 0
def spectralIndex {n} (X : Mat n) : ℝ := n * Matrix.trace X

theorem lift_pair {n} (X : Kirchhoff.Mat n) : pairIndex (liftQ X) = algebraMap ℚ ℝ (Kirchhoff.pairIndex X) := by
 simp [pairIndex, Kirchhoff.pairIndex, liftQ, map_sum, apply_ite]
theorem lift_spec {n} (X : Kirchhoff.Mat n) : spectralIndex (liftQ X) = algebraMap ℚ ℝ (Kirchhoff.spectralIndex X) := by
 unfold spectralIndex Kirchhoff.spectralIndex Matrix.trace
 rw [map_mul, map_natCast, map_sum]
 rfl

def LiteralConjecture (Inv : {n : ℕ} → Mat n → Mat n → Prop)
 (R : {n : ℕ} → Mat n → ℝ) : Prop :=
 ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → ∀ g : Kirchhoff.Graph n, g.simple.Connected → ∀ a : ℤ, a = 1 ∨ a = -1 →
 ∃ X0 Xa : Mat n, Inv (liftQ (Kirchhoff.laplacian g 0)) X0 ∧
 Inv (liftQ (Kirchhoff.laplacian g a)) Xa ∧
 (if a = 1 then R X0 ≤ R Xa else R Xa ≤ R X0) ∧
 (R Xa = R X0 ↔ Kirchhoff.Regular g)

theorem refuteMP : ¬ LiteralConjecture @Penrose @pairIndex := by
 intro h
 obtain ⟨X0,X1,h0,h1,hle,_⟩ := h 11 (by decide) Kirchhoff.witness Kirchhoff.witness_connected 1 (Or.inl rfl)
 rw [Kirchhoff.lapZero] at h0
 rw [Kirchhoff.lapOne] at h1
 have e0 := penrose_unique h0 (lift_penrose Kirchhoff.validMPZero)
 have e1 := penrose_unique h1 (lift_penrose Kirchhoff.validMPOne)
 simp only [ite_true, e0, e1, lift_pair, Kirchhoff.mp0, Kirchhoff.mp1] at hle
 norm_num at hle

theorem refuteSpec : ¬ LiteralConjecture @GroupInverse @spectralIndex := by
 intro h
 obtain ⟨X0,X1,h0,h1,hle,_⟩ := h 11 (by decide) Kirchhoff.witness Kirchhoff.witness_connected 1 (Or.inl rfl)
 rw [Kirchhoff.lapZero] at h0
 rw [Kirchhoff.lapOne] at h1
 have e0 := group_unique h0 (lift_group Kirchhoff.validGIZero)
 have e1 := group_unique h1 (lift_group Kirchhoff.validGIOne)
 simp only [ite_true, e0, e1, lift_spec, Kirchhoff.gi0, Kirchhoff.gi1] at hle
 norm_num at hle
end KirchhoffReal

{"title":"A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering","subtitle":"DRAFT | MathDB 349441 | 2 November 2026 UTC","sections":[

{"title":"2. Why the three source descriptions separate","sections":[

from fractions import Fraction as F
import json,hashlib
D=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
f=D/'sources/kirchhoff-review-r1/outputs/witness-exact.json';data=json.loads(f.read_text())
n=11
I=[[F(i==j) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
def mul(A,B):return [[sum(A[i][k]*B[k][j] for k in range(n)) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
def tr(A):return [[A[j][i] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
deg=[6]+[5]*5+[2]*4+[1]
edges={(i,j) for i in range(6) for j in range(i+1,6)}|{(0,6),(6,7),(7,8),(8,9),(9,10)}
results={}
for alpha,row in data.items():
 a=int(alpha);mpval,specval,mat=row
 A,M,G=[[[F(x) for x in r] for r in mat[k]] for k in ['L','MP','GI']]
 L=[[F(0) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
 for i,j in edges:
  for u,v in [(i,j),(j,i)]:L[u][v]=-F(deg[u],deg[v])**a;L[u][u]-=L[u][v]
 assert A==L
 AM,MA=mul(A,M),mul(M,A)
 assert mul(AM,A)==A and mul(MA,M)==M and tr(AM)==AM and tr(MA)==MA
 AG,GA=mul(A,G),mul(G,A)
 assert mul(AG,A)==A and mul(GA,G)==G and AG==GA
 pair=sum(M[i][i]+M[j][j]-M[i][j]-M[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1,n))
 spec=n*sum(G[i][i] for i in range(n))
 assert pair==F(mpval) and spec==F(specval)
 results[alpha]={'MP':str(pair),'spectral':str(spec),'equations':'PASS'}
assert F(370,3)-F(1696684,14035)==F(102898,42105)>0
(D/'receipts/exact-cross-check.json').write_text(json.dumps({'status':'PASS','source_sha256':hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'values':results},indent=2)+'\n')

# Statement correspondence

| Source or binding ruling | Lean object and justification |
| --- | --- |
| Finite simple graphs, at least two vertices | `Kirchhoff.Graph n`, Boolean adjacency with symmetry and no loops; `Graph.simple` is a mathlib `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`; both conjectures quantify over every `n ≥ 2` and every connected such graph. Boolean adjacency loses no finite decidable graph. |
| Degree and K to the power alpha | `degree` sums adjacency indicators; `Kpow` is diagonal with integer powers of the rational degree. |
| Equation (3.8) | `laplacian`; `laplacian_source_formula` proves it equals diagonal row weights minus `Kpow g a * adjacency g * Kpow g (-a)`. All integer alpha values are defined; the conjectures restrict alpha to 1 or -1. Real entries are the exact scalar extension of these rational entries. |
| Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse | `Penrose` contains all four equations, including both transpose equations. `penrose_unique` proves uniqueness over Q, and `KirchhoffReal.penrose_unique` over R. `validMPZero` and `validMPOne` exhibit existence at the witness; `lift_penrose` transfers every equation to R. |
| Equation (4.3), primary | `pairIndex` sums `Xii + Xjj - Xij - Xji` over `i < j`. `resistance_sum` also identifies the sum of the graph-level `resistance`. Neither inverse is assumed symmetric. |
| Definition 4.5 | `indexMP` is the sum from (4.3). `LiteralConjecture` also states the source directly with existential inverse data, removing any dependence on choice defaults. The existential data are unique by the proved uniqueness theorem. |
| Lemma 4.6, secondary | `GroupInverse` contains AXA=A, XAX=X, AX=XA; `group_unique` proves uniqueness over Q and R. `spectralIndex` is n times the trace of that unique group inverse, as permitted by the binding ruling. No unproved eigenvalue bridge is used. |
| Conjecture 4.13 | `KirchhoffReal.LiteralConjecture` states universal ordering for alpha in {1,-1} and equality iff regular, with existence of the inverses explicit. `KirchhoffReal.refuteMP` and `.refuteSpec` negate the two readings. Rational counterparts and choice-based index formulations are also proved false. |
| Witness | `witness` is K6 on 0 through 5, with edges 0–6–7–8–9–10. `witness_connected`, `witness_degrees`, `lapZero`, and `lapOne` establish the graph-to-certificate bridge. |
| Physical Definition 4.1 | Not the endpoint. The binding ruling finds the all-pairs potential interpretation ill-posed on nonregular graphs. We use the two algebraic readings exactly as ruled, without asserting equivalence to that physical definition. |

The existential formulations do not assume a global inverse existence theorem. They state existence as part of the universal source assertion and refute its ordering at a graph where existence and uniqueness are both proved. The auxiliary `mp`/`gi` selectors have a zero default outside their existence predicates; the primary real endpoints do not depend on these selectors or their defaults.
